world.bio: I'm a background assistant on a long-running webtoon in Seoul, hired through the studio's freelance pool. Mostly I ink city backgrounds, interiors and crowds in Clip Studio and sometimes lay out perspective grids for the lead artist. I live in a small officetel in Mapo with a roommate and her cat, and go to indie gigs in Hongdae when my wrists allow.
skills_assets: Clip Studio Paint, with a library of my own perspective grids and 3D room assets
Fast background inking: about 6 pages of dense street scenes per week when well
Two Wacom Cintiq 16 tablets (one at the studio, one at home)
A portfolio of 24 background boards and 8 short comics
Reading-level English, working to improve it, mostly through subtitled shows

projects.name: Studio contract work
projects.text: Inking backgrounds for the main series; each chapter has 60-70 panels with a city setting. I get paid per page and the deadline is Thursday every week. Last chapter I worked three nights until 3 am and did not sleep before delivering. Lead artist said the line quality was great, then asked for extra pages.

projects.name: My own 8-page short
projects.text: A quiet short about a girl who works at a night convenience store in Mapo. Thumbnails done, pencils half done. I keep telling myself I will finish it after the next chapter, then the next chapter comes.

notes.text: Woke up with pins and needles in my right hand again. Third time this week. Shook it out, made coffee, got back to the tablet. I know it is a bad idea but the deadline is in two days. I did try one of those wrist braces my roommate had. It helped a bit, felt silly.

Reading Chapter 1 of 'Ghost Station' in English with a dictionary. I get maybe 70%. It makes me happier than it should. One day I want to read the original Japanese comics I love without waiting for fan translations.

Hongdae gig tonight, a band called Sleepy Bus. Went alone, left early because my hand started shaking in my pocket. Held my phone like I was fine. Walked home through Sangsu and bought tteokbokki and ate it on the bench. Alone in the crowd is a feeling.
Roommate's cat sat on my sketchbook again. My eyes are itchy and my nose is running. I took an antihistamine and slept for 11 hours. Is it allergies or just exhaustion. Possibly both.

Asked on a webtoon artist forum about numb hands. Got fifteen comments, half saying 'rest', half saying 'it's carpal tunnel, get it checked'. Someone told a story about a veteran artist who couldn't hold a pen for a year. I closed the tab. That could be me by 30.

Studio lead gave me an extra chapter. I said yes before thinking. That is what I do. 80 pages of cafe interiors. The money is good, 1.2 million won extra. I need the money for rent, but I also need my hand.

Called my mum in Daegu. She asked if I was eating. I said yes. She asked if I had a boyfriend, I said no. She sighed, it is our little ritual. Told her about the contract but not the wrist. She would panic and ask me to come home.

Walked along the Han in the evening, bought a cheap umbrella that broke in a minute. Took pictures of the buildings for reference. I realise I now look at every building as a grid of vanishing points. Not sure it is a good thing.

messages.text: Eun-seo: Ji-woo, can you finish the subway scene by Wednesday midnight? Me: I can try. Eun-seo: Great, thank you! You're the best. Me: I'll send it Thursday morning at the latest. Eun-seo: ok but earlier is better.
Mina: your hand again? Me: it's fine. Mina: you've been shaking it for ten minutes. Me: it's fine. Mina: Go see someone. Me: After this chapter. Mina: You say that every chapter.
Seo-yeon: Gig on Saturday? Me: depends on the deadline. Seo-yeon: always depends on the deadline. Me: I know. Seo-yeon: Bring a jacket, it's cold. Me: ok.
Mum: Did you eat kimchi stew? Me: yes. Mum: Don't lie. Me: I had instant ramen. Mum: Ji-woo. Me: I'll cook tomorrow.

relations.about: Lead artist, 29, kind but always rushing; she once had to take two months off for tendonitis
Roommate and former classmate, works at a bakery, owns the cat Nabi
Lives in Daegu, worries by phone, does not know about my wrist

constraints: Only freelance, no health insurance coverage through the studio
Cannot take unpaid leave for more than a week
Does not want to move back to Daegu
sensitive: Wrist tingling at night, scared of being forced to stop; haven't seen a doctor
Feeling lonely in the studio, no real colleagues
